title: Control plane: emit v1 audit events for RBAC CRUD endpoints
author: Benji Okafor
body: Context: We’re standardizing audit logging across Hosted/Dedicated/Private with a canonical v1 schema. RBAC is a top-tier sensitive surface (role definitions, role bindings, membership changes), and we’ve had customer reports of missing RBAC change events in Private (SUP-18421). This PR instruments the control plane RBAC service (and the HTTP layer that fronts it) to emit v1 audit events for RBAC CRUD actions with consistent actor attribution, safe diff summaries, and correlation IDs (request_id/trace_id/admin_action_id) for investigations. What’s included: (1) v1 audit event emission for RBAC endpoints: role.create, role.update, role.delete; role_binding.create/update/delete; membership add/remove; project/tenant-scoped permission bundle updates. (2) Actor identity + impersonation support: actor.type (user|service_account|service), actor.id, actor.email (when available), actor.session_id, actor.impersonated_by.* (when admin impersonation is used), and source_ip/user_agent pulled from request context. (3) Diff summaries for update operations: we generate a constrained JSON Patch-style diff (ops limited + size capped) and also include a human-friendly summary string for common RBAC changes (“added permission: models.use”, “removed member: user:abc”). (4) Correlation: request_id + trace_id propagated from gateway headers, plus admin_action_id generated for Console-initiated workflows and included in both the HTTP response and emitted audit events. (5) Safety + operability: audit emission is best-effort (does not block RBAC writes on sink failure) but increments metrics and logs structured errors; payload fields are classified and redacted (no secrets; free-form strings truncated; role descriptions not included in diffs). Testing: unit tests for diff generator + actor extraction; integration tests that exercise RBAC endpoints and assert a schema-valid v1 audit event is emitted via the in-memory audit sink. Example emitted event (redacted): {"schema_version":"1.0","event_type":"rbac.role.update","event_id":"01HRQ0...","occurred_at":"2026-02-03T19:22:11.482Z","tenant_id":"tnt_9f3...","project_id":"prj_12a...","actor.type":"user","actor.id":"usr_3c1...","actor.email":"admin@customer.com","actor.ip":"203.0.113.10","actor.impersonated_by.id":"usr_8aa...","request_id":"req_7b1...","trace_id":"9b2f...","admin_action_id":"admact_17c...","target.type":"rbac.role","target.id":"role_29d...","change.summary":"added permission: routing.policy.write","change.diff":"[{\"op\":\"add\",\"path\":\"/permissions/4\",\"value\":\"routing.policy.write\"}]"}. Rollout notes: guarded behind feature flag AUDIT_V1_RBAC_ENABLED (default on in staging, off in prod until exporter normalization is deployed); legacy audit events (pre-v1) are left unchanged for now (ENG-4833 handles normalization/deprecation). Follow-ups: Console needs to pass admin_action_id consistently for all RBAC admin flows; Private parity tracked in the installer/exporter workstreams. Checklist: - [x] Event types registered in taxonomy registry - [x] Required fields present per schema v1 - [x] No PII/secrets logged; diff capped and validated - [x] Metrics for emit failures added - [x] Integration tests added and running in CI
commits: control-plane/rbac: add AuditContext extractor (actor, source, correlation IDs)
control-plane/rbac: emit v1 audit events for role CRUD
control-plane/rbac: emit v1 audit events for role bindings + membership changes
control-plane/audit: add constrained diff generator for RBAC updates
tests: add RBAC audit event integration tests using in-memory audit sink
metrics: audit emit error counter + latency histogram tags
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can we guarantee request_id/trace_id are always set for internal callers (e.g., migrations / cron)? If missing, what do we emit?

Benji Okafor (author): Added defaults in AuditContext: request_id generated when absent; trace_id optional (empty string omitted). For internal jobs, actor.type=service and actor.id set to the job name; added tests for missing incoming headers.
Hanae Suzuki (review): Diff payload looks like it could include role descriptions (free text). We should avoid emitting arbitrary strings to SIEMs; also ensure truncation is enforced.

Benji Okafor (author): Agreed. Removed role.description from diff inputs entirely; only include permissions + bindings + members. Diff generator now hard-caps at 25 ops and 4KB, truncates values, and falls back to change.summary when over budget.
Allison Grant (review): Please tag audit emit failures with service + event_type but avoid high-cardinality labels (tenant_id/project_id). Also confirm best-effort behavior won’t break RBAC writes.

Benji Okafor (author): Updated metrics labels to {service,event_type,result}. No tenant/project labels. Emission errors are logged + metered but do not block handler execution; tests cover sink failure path.
Marcus Lin (review): This references SUP-18421. Are we covering the specific missing events (role binding changes) and do we have a way to correlate Console actions across multiple calls?

Benji Okafor (author): Yes—role_binding create/update/delete and membership add/remove included. admin_action_id is generated for Console-initiated flows and returned as a response header so subsequent calls can reuse it; Console follow-up tracked separately but control plane supports it now.
Ethan Park (review): Ship it after the diff cap change. Approved.
Hanae Suzuki (review): Approved after redaction changes; thanks.
release_notes: Control plane RBAC endpoints now emit audit log schema v1 events for role and binding changes with consistent actor attribution and correlation IDs.
